head: Rule
Works when
Fails when
rows: Confirm identity before comparing versions.
An item and the record can be unambiguously matched.
Labels are missing or reused.
Choose control boundaries by consequence.
Independent versions or interfaces matter.
Every low-impact detail receives a separate approval queue.
Use an accepted version as the reference.
The owner and revision are known.
The "latest" document is an unfinished draft.
Do not confuse requested with authorized.
A proposal is still under review.
A project exception process provides a different but still accountable route.
Keep authorization distinct from execution.
Units can receive modifications at different times.
A board decision is reported as installed work.
Release a consistent set of related documents.
A change affects more than one file.
An obsolete instruction remains in circulation.
Treat missing data as unknown.
Status records are incomplete.
An empty field is silently counted as unchanged.
Match each audit question with relevant evidence.
Tests and build records have different purposes.
A passed test is used to excuse a build mismatch.
Keep findings until their disposition is demonstrated.
Corrective action can be tracked.
A conditional approval hides an unresolved item.

rows: You cannot explain who controls a version.
